title: Network-Science-Informed Speed-Up of Shortest-Path Counting Boosts Betweenness Centrality and Geometrical Congruence Computation
content: Connectivity laws conserved across systems, independently of edge weights, are compelling in network science. Many network metrics aggregate information counting all shortest-paths between node pairs, which is costly. Here we formalize the all-pairs shortest-path number (APSPN) problem and establish a shared computational foundation for these kinds of problems, including betweenness centrality (BC) and geometrical congruence (GC). We introduce the CC-APSPN kernel, which exploits network science principles to accelerate their shared computations on unweighted graphs via knowledge memoization, reducing runtime by up to 90% over the Brandes-APSPN baseline across diverse network topologies. Parallel CC-APSPN carries this acceleration onto multicore CPUs through batched source processing with a dedicated scheduling strategy, reducing exact BC and GC runtimes from hours to a few minutes on a 100,000-node network. Besides, we propose CC-bbBFS, a single-pair primitive for efficient sampling-based approximation of BC and GC. Together, these advances translate network-science-informed algorithm design into practical large-scale analysis.
